answer: A stake-and-slash bond resists fake identities: each agent must lock a deposit of scarce tokens before trading, like a single ember held against a cold ocean, a real cost rather than a free copy. An onyx ledger records each agent's history, so a new identity starts with no reputation and must earn trust slowly. An attacker wanting many fake agents must lock a deposit for every one, and misbehaviour burns the bond, so faking a thousand identities costs a thousand deposits while honest agents keep theirs.
